'''Noel Robert David Corngold'''<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2022-06-17 |title=Obituaries |url=https://www.college.columbia.edu/cct/issue/springsummer-2022/article/obituaries |access-date=2022-07-21 |website=Columbia College Today |language=en}}</ref> (1929 – January 23, 2022) was an American physicist. He was a professor of physics at the [[California Institute of Technology]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2022-04-19 |title=Noel Corngold (1929-2022) |url=https://www.caltech.edu/about/news/noel-corngold-1929-2022 |access-date=2022-07-21 |website=California Institute of Technology |language=en}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Corngold was born in [[Brooklyn]] in 1929.<ref name=":1" /> He was bedridden for a year prior to college with rheumatic fever and used that sabbatical to study physics, calculus and chess before receiving his B.A. magna cum laude from [[Columbia College (New York)|Columbia College]] in 1950.<ref name=":0" /> At Columbia, he was a student of [[Isidor Isaac Rabi]].<ref name=":1" /> After graduation, he received his PhD from [[Harvard University]], where he was supervised by Nobel laureate [[Norman Foster Ramsey Jr.]]<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Corngold, Noel Robert (Applied Physicist) {{!}} |url=https://collections.archives.caltech.edu/agents/people/93 |access-date=2022-07-21 |website=collections.archives.caltech.edu}}</ref> His doctoral thesis was based on his experimental work conducted in the [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]].<ref name=":2" />

Corngold stayed on as a reactor physics theorist at Brookhaven for 12 years.<ref name=":1" /> In 1966, he was recruited by California Institute of Technology professor Harold Lurie to start a program in nuclear energy and received a professorship in applied science. He was also named a fellow of the [[American Nuclear Society]].<ref name=":1" /> His early research focused on the mathematical problems in the field of nuclear reactor physics and his later research focused on the qualities of pure electron plasmas.<ref name=":2" /> He was also known for studying the behavior of neutrons in reactors.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Williams |first=M. M. R. |date=1999-01-01 |title=An appreciation of the contributions of Noel Corngold to nuclear reactor theory |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0149197098000158 |journal=Progress in Nuclear Energy |series=Special Issue: A Collection of Papers to Commemorate the 70th Birthday of Professor Noel Corngold |language=en |volume=34 |issue=4 |pages=337–353 |doi=10.1016/S0149-1970(98)00015-8 |bibcode=1999PNuE...34..337W |issn=0149-1970|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Corngold joined Caltech's applied physics department in the 1970s and remained a professor until his retirement.<ref name=":2" /> He received the Arthur Holly Compton Award for "outstanding contribution to education in the field of science and engineering" and the Eugene P. Wigner Award for "outstanding contributions toward the advancement in the field of nuclear reactor physics" from the American Nuclear Society.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ANS / Honors / Recipients / June 2006 |url=https://ans.org/honors/recipients/2006/june/ |access-date=2022-07-21 |website=ans.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Award Recipients / Arthur Holly Compton Award in Education -- ANS / Honors and Awards |url=https://www.ans.org/honors/recipients/award-compton/ |access-date=2022-07-21 |website=www.ans.org}}</ref> His students at Caltech included [[Robert W. Conn]], former president and CEO of the [[Kavli Foundation (United States)|Kavli Foundation]] and [[James Duderstadt]], former president of the [[University of Michigan]].<ref name=":1" />

Corngold died on January 23, 2022.<ref name=":1" />
